name: Directional Influence (DI)
goal: Change your launch angle with the control stick
why: DI sets the direction a hit launches you. Against a strong sideways hit, holding the control stick up and toward the stage raises the launch angle by up to 18 degrees, so {char} reaches the side blast zone later and survives to a higher percent; against an upward hit, holding it to the side turns the launch away from the top. With no DI the same hit kills earlier.

tutorial.what: DI is the control stick's direction on the last frame of hitlag. The game turns the launch angle toward it by up to 18 degrees.
tutorial.expect: {opp} plays footsies, comes to its distance and attacks: another attack every try. {char}'s damage is drawn for each try, around the damage the attack kills at. Each hit is judged on the first frame of the launch: whether the control stick was held on the last frame of hitlag, and the angle {char} moved at. Gravity makes that angle a few degrees lower than the hit's own.

marks.2: Frame 2: the control stick is held {way}
marks.HL: Frame {HL}: the last frame of hitlag. The game reads the stick
marks.HL+1: Frame {HL+1}: launched at about {FULL} degrees instead of {ANGLE}

lessons.title: Hitlag
text: When a hit connects, both fighters freeze: hitlag. Its length comes from the hit's damage: a third of the damage plus 3 frames, rounded down. The opponent's forward smash deals 15, so hitlag lasts 8 frames.
{char} cannot move during hitlag, but the game still reads the control stick. Knockback starts on the frame after hitlag.

lessons.title: How DI works
text: The game reads the control stick on the last frame of hitlag and turns the launch angle toward it by 18 degrees times the square of the stick's component perpendicular to the launch. Perpendicular gives all 18; along the launch line, none.
The forward smash launches {char} at 44 degrees. Up and toward the opponent is perpendicular to that and turns it to about 62. Straight up, 46 degrees off the line, turns it about 9.

marks.1: Frame 1: the forward smash hits. Hitlag begins
marks.2: Frame {f}: hitlag. The stick is held up and toward the opponent
marks.8: Frame 8: the last frame of hitlag. The game reads the stick
marks.9: Frame 9: launched about 18 degrees higher than with no DI

cues.words: Hitlag: hold the stick up and toward the opponent
Last frame of hitlag: the stick is read now

lessons.title: Upward hits
text: Fox's up smash launches {char} at 80 degrees: nearly straight up, leaning away from Fox. Perpendicular to that is to the side.

Held away from Fox, the control stick turns the launch about 18 degrees lower, away from the top blast zone. Held up or down, along the launch, it turns nothing. Every hit has its own angle, and its own DI.

marks.2: Frame {f}: hitlag. The stick is held away from Fox
marks.9: Frame 9: the last frame of hitlag. The game reads the stick
marks.10: Frame 10: launched lower than the up smash's 80 degrees

cues.words: Hitlag: hold the stick away from Fox
Last frame of hitlag: the stick is read now

attempt.missed: Not counted: {move} did not hit. Hold your ground: {opp} comes to its distance and attacks.

stick held.expect: Control stick held on the last frame of hitlag
stick held.words: the control stick was in neutral on the last frame of hitlag
stick held.headline: No DI
stick held.fix: Tilt the control stick during hitlag and keep it there until {char} is launched. The game reads it only on the last frame of hitlag; a stick let go before then is no DI.

raised.expect: Launch turned the way that survives
raised.words: launched at {launch} degrees; about {ANGLE} with no DI
raised.headline: DI the wrong way
raised.fix: Hold the control stick {way}: it turns the launch {turn}. {wrong}

full DI.expect: Launch turned most of the 18 degrees
full DI.words: launched at {launch} degrees; full DI gives about {FULL}
full DI.headline: Not perpendicular
full DI.fix: Hold the control stick {way}, perpendicular to the launch. A stick 45 degrees off it gives about half of the 18 degrees.
